label: Square Side Adjust Button
note: Owner-uploaded reference images. Authoritative for construction/appearance; NOT usable as the tech-pack illustration (not line art, or shows multiple options).

references.evidence: 474x315 px close-up colour photo of the side of a dark navy trouser waistband worn under a grey knit. At 5x I can count three 4-hole shell buttons in a horizontal row on the waistband; the right-hand button sits on a squared-off cloth tab whose outline and edge stitching are visible on all four sides, with a short horizontal buttonhole slit just outboard of that button. Below the waistband seam are the trouser front pleat/crease lines. No metal slider, no visible elastic, no buckle.
references.ownerNotes: the allistic is hidden inside the waistband

references.evidence: 267x332 px close-up colour photo of the side waistband of grey wool trousers worn with a blue shirt, the wearer's hand at top of frame. At 7x the adjuster reads clearly: a near-square cloth tab (about as tall as it is wide, squared corners, edge stitching visible on all four sides) applied to the waistband with a dark 4-hole button centred on it, and two further buttons sewn on the waistband outboard of the tab providing the adjustment positions. Waistband seam, side seam, front crease and a slanted pocket opening also visible. No metal slider, no buckle, no exposed elastic.
